scope: Latency baseline of the PUBLIC read operations of the OpenTransit scheduled API, measured against an already-running local Docker Desktop stack on a Windows 11 developer machine over loopback (127.0.0.1:8000, HTTP/1.1, no TLS, no load balancer). The API container has a 1 GiB memory limit and no CPU limit on a 16-CPU Docker VM; MOTIS (2 GiB cap) and Photon (1 GiB cap) run in sibling containers. Sequential keep-alive client, paced under the API's per-client rate limiter; a few hundred requests per group. NOT a load test, NOT Fargate (no 8 GiB serving cap, no vCPU limits, no network hop), NOT acceptance evidence, NOT a capacity statement. Read-only: only ordinary API requests, docker logs/stats/inspect and one docker exec running read-only MOTIS plan calls.

provenance.scripts: Scratchpad (not in repo): ot.py (keep-alive http.client + client-side token pacer), run.py, analyze.py (joins client samples to docker logs by X-Request-ID), direct_motis.py, loopblock.py. Raw samples: 1365 requests in run.py plus 20 in loopblock.py.

method: Client: Python http.client, one persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection per thread, Accept-Encoding: gzip, br sent on every request, client_ms = perf_counter around request+full body read.

Pacing: the per-client limiter (default 60/min standard, 30/min expensive, in-process, keyed by client IP; Docker Desktop NAT makes all host clients one identity) forced <= ~0.85 req/s on standard routes and <= ~0.42 req/s on /v1/places and /v1/journeys, so sample counts are 6-40 per variant, not thousands. No 429 occurred (n429=0). /healthz and /readyz are exempt and were sampled 300 and 40 times.

Server time: route log line request_id=<X-Request-ID> route=... duration_ms=... (SafeRequests middleware, wraps the whole app incl. serialization, excludes uvicorn socket read/write and client). Joined by X-Request-ID; every sample in the table joined. /v1/places also has stopsearch log lines (search_ms) and geocoder phase lines (backend_ms, normalize_ms); the geocoder lines carry no backend name, so 'slowest geocoder backend' is max over the request's phase lines (MOTIS PLACE for poi, Photon for address, none for stop/station).

Cold vs warm: 'firstCallClientMs' is the first request of that variant in this run (the stack had been up for days, so it is not a process-cold start, but MOTIS/SQLite/OS page caches and per-query caches were cold for that exact input); 'repeatClientMsExclFirst' excludes it. For /v1/places each variant is 4 distinct queries x 2 repeats, so the repeat half is a same-query repeat.
Floor: /healthz p50 on keep-alive with no I/O gives framework + middleware + uvicorn cost; /v1/stops with no selector (422) and an unmatched 404 add routing/validation/problem-JSON.

MOTIS split: docker exec -i ot-demo-api python - sent 8 GET /api/v6/plan calls per case directly to 127.0.0.1:8080 with the adapter's parameter set (services/api/src/opentransit/motis.py) except transitModes=TRANSIT rather than the API's bus/rail/light_rail expansion (so direct payloads are larger: n3 Savidor->Haifa 68.5 KB direct vs 24.5 KB API). Treat the difference as an upper-bound estimate of API-side work, not an exact split.

Event-loop probe: a second thread pinged /healthz every ~5 ms (exempt from the limiter) while one request of the type under test ran; the maximum healthz latency during that request shows how long the single event loop was unavailable. 4 repetitions per type.
Concurrency probe: N threads, each with its own connection, released together; 5 rounds per N; round wall time is first-start to last-finish.

fixedFloor.readSentence: Framework+middleware+uvicorn on a keep-alive loopback connection is about 0.6-0.8 ms client round trip (0.2 ms inside the middleware). The ~12 ms seen on a single cold curl is a new Docker Desktop TCP connection, not the app. An invalid /v1/stops (422) costs 2.3 ms client / 0.7 ms server and an unmatched path 1.7 / 0.3 ms.

journeyEngineSplit.apiWarmJourneyServerMs: TA Dizengoff->Ramat Gan r3 p50 30.7 (first 567) ; Savidor->Haifa r1 29.8 ; r3 67.9 ; r5 98.7 ; Jerusalem->TA r3 43.4
journeyEngineSplit.readSentence: Warm direct MOTIS plan (same params, TRANSIT): short TA ~12-13 ms, Savidor->Haifa n1 ~20 ms, n3 ~50 ms, n5 ~77 ms, Jerusalem->TA n3 ~29 ms. API server time for the same queries is 30 / 30 / 68 / 99 / 43 ms, i.e. roughly 10-20 ms (n1: ~10 ms, n3/n5: ~18-22 ms, short n3: ~18 ms) of API-side work sits on top of the engine, scaling with itinerary count; this includes JSON parse of a larger direct payload, normalization, Pydantic validation and serialization of the 24-36 KB response, plus the loopback HTTP hop. Engine share of warm API journey time is roughly 40% (short TA) to 78% (n5 Savidor->Haifa).

observations: MEASURED: single-record reference lookups are slow. GET /v1/stops/{id} (server p50 480-510 ms), GET /v1/routes/{id} (470 ms) and GET /v1/routes/{id}/patterns (470 ms) cost ~470-510 ms server time for tiny responses (2.6-3.5 KB for ordinary stops/routes), essentially independent of response size or entity, while list queries on the same SQLite file are fast (stops near r500 7 ms, routes?operatorId 8 ms, /v1/trips/{ref} 8 ms). INFERRED (code read at fe5df53, plan not run): ReferenceDB.stop()/route() call _translations(), whose WHERE has an OR branch (record_id='' AND field_value=?) while the only translations index is (record_id, lang); the branch cannot use it, so each call plausibly scans the translations table. Not confirmed with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (that would have required a DB read outside the permitted operations). Every public call that resolves a stop reference pays it.

MEASURED: that cost leaks into operations that look cheap. GET /v1/stops/{id}/departures server p50 588-972 ms (37358 h60 678 ms, 35832 h60 587 ms, 13583 default h120 971 ms) and 21 of 80 departures requests failed 504 ENGINE_TIMEOUT at the 1.5 s deadline (all 20 of 13583 h1440 limit100, plus 1 of the h120 run). POST /v1/journeys with kind=stop inputs: server p50 1,510 ms, 5 of 8 returned 504 (the other 3 succeeded near the deadline); the same trip with coordinate inputs is 68 ms p50. A standalone stop-id journey in the event-loop probe took ~975 ms (200). INFERRED from code: journeys call reference.stop() synchronously for both ends (motis.py _engine_place) and departures call it once (motis_timetable.py), i.e. ~2x and ~1x the ~480 ms lookup, consistent with ~975 ms and ~590-680 ms.

MEASURED: those paths block the single event loop. While one departures request ran, concurrent /healthz max latency was 421-486 ms (4/4 reps); during a stop-id journey it was 932-962 ms (4/4 reps). While GET /v1/stops/{id} (sync def handler, threadpool) ran, healthz max was only ~16 ms; during a coordinate journey max ~2-25 ms; during a stop-search /v1/places max ~17-23 ms (stop search runs in asyncio.to_thread). So a single departures or stop-id journey stalls every other in-flight request on the worker for 0.4-1.0 s, including /readyz health probes. INFERRED: synchronous SQLite inside async handlers is the cause (the places route is the only one using to_thread).

MEASURED: /v1/places stop/station search is the largest cost in typeahead: server p50 for 2-char prefixes is 218 ms (he) and 411 ms (en) for stop+station, and ~210 ms p95 even for 3- and 5-char Hebrew prefixes on first sight of a query; the same query repeated is ~1 ms (stopSearchMs min 0.6-1.0 ms; the p95 of ~210 ms is the first-sight half of each variant), so a per-query result cache or memo is plausible (not confirmed in code). 2-character prefixes are NOT helped by repetition (he min 208 ms, en min 397 ms for search_ms): they stay at 200-440 ms on every call. Full-name stop queries are 3-9 ms. Default all-types requests inherit the slowest of stop search and the geocoders: he prefix2 p50 274 ms, en prefix2 p50 420 ms (of which MOTIS geocoder ~296 ms p50 and stop search ~417 ms; non-backend remainder 114 ms p50). The Hebrew MOTIS PLACE geocoder tail noted in m4-latency-diagnosis-20261001-02 is still visible: he poi full queries p50 56 ms server (backend ~54 ms) versus en poi full 8 ms; one direct in-container MOTIS /api/v1/geocode for 'דיזנגוף סנטר' (type=PLACE) took ~20 ms x8, but the table averages four different multi-token queries, so the two are not directly comparable.

MEASURED: geocoder sidecars are not the dominant cost for short queries: Photon address-only p50 14-26 ms, MOTIS PLACE poi p50 3-12 ms (en) / 7-56 ms (he, full). The API's own non-backend time for single-geocoder requests is ~0.7-1.1 ms. No geocoderUnavailable events (0) occurred in this run, but see next item.

MEASURED: the first journey after an idle period timed out. My very first POST /v1/journeys (Savidor->Haifa coordinates) returned 504 ENGINE_TIMEOUT after 1.22 s, the subsequent three identical calls took 91-118 ms. A places query with an address type also hit the 1.2 s Photon deadline (outcome=unavailable, 1.22 s) on its first call. Both preceded the formal run (during discovery) and are not in the tables; the log shows readiness_failed reasons=engine:ENGINE_TIMEOUT once earlier in the container's life. Cause inferred: cold MOTIS/Photon memory-mapped data after idle; the bind mount lives on D:, behind Docker Desktop's file-sharing layer.

MEASURED: first-call penalty is large and systematic for journeys. For 8 identical requests per variant, first call (client ms) -> repeat p50 (server ms): short TA 567 -> 31, Haifa short 438 -> 31, Jerusalem short 820 -> 22, Navon->Savidor 756 -> 43, HaShalom->Beersheba 574 -> 33, Modiin->T3 451 -> 39, Savidor->Haifa r3 173 -> 68. After the first call the repeat p95 is within ~1.5x of p50; the 'p95' in these 8-sample rows is therefore the first call. These are cold-per-input costs (MOTIS routing page-in) and recur for every novel origin/destination pair, so warm repeated queries understate real user latency. A real-use distribution needs many distinct pairs.

MEASURED: journey time scales with itinerary count and distance: Savidor->Haifa results=1/3/5 -> server p50 29.8 / 67.9 / 98.7 ms with responses of 6.5 / 24.5 / 35.8 KB. modes=rail (852 B, effectively empty) 12.9 ms, arriveBy 32 ms, no_route 9.5 ms. The default results=3 costs ~2.3x results=1.

MEASURED: concurrency. One uvicorn worker (docker top). Journeys do NOT serialize: 1/2/4 concurrent same-query journeys had round wall p50 65 / 76 / 88 ms (4x the work in 1.4x the time), mixed-query journeys 27 / 66 / 71 ms; the MOTIS call is awaited asynchronously and MOTIS uses several cores. /v1/places is closer to linear: stop-only en 1 vs 4 concurrent round wall 7.6 -> 29 ms (3.8x), address-only (Photon) 13.3 -> 36 ms (2.7x), i.e. stop search (thread + GIL) and the JSON/merge work behave like a serial section. The only truly blocking calls found are the sync-SQLite async handlers above. Not measured: more than 4 concurrent, sustained load, memory growth, PLANNING_CONCURRENCY=16 behaviour.

MEASURED: /v1/status and /readyz are not free: server p50 17.4 ms (/v1/status, 797 B) and 14.9 ms (/readyz, p95 31 ms, 100 B) versus 0.2 ms for /healthz. If an ALB/Fargate health check or a client polls these frequently they cost real worker time and (per the blocking finding) wait behind blocked loops. Source of the 15-17 ms not examined.

MEASURED: list-style reference endpoints are cheap and linear in rows: stops near r500 limit20 server p50 7.4 ms (8.3 KB), r2000 limit100 19.7 ms (37.6 KB), bbox TA centre limit100 17 ms (34 KB); routes?routeShortName 5.7 ms, routes?operatorId limit100 8.3 ms (26.8 KB), /v1/trips/{ref} 7.5-8 ms (2.3-4.5 KB). routes?stopId= is 114-179 ms (EXISTS join on route_stops), another stop-id-resolving path. A wide bbox (0.2 x 0.25 deg) returned 422 INVALID_REQUEST (15/15) and is not part of the table results; the accepted bbox shape is west,south,east,north with south<north<=34 etc., my wide box was probably rejected by an area limit (not investigated).

MEASURED: payload and protocol. No compression is offered, no validators exist (no ETag/Last-Modified), responses are no-store, HTTP/1.1 only. Responses repeated byte-identically within one generation (e.g. stop 37358, 181 KB) cannot be revalidated or cached by clients/CDN; on a metered path every byte goes out raw.

MEASURED: unexplained stall. During the floor run, 5 of 30 sequential invalid-/v1/stops 422 requests took 9-1013 ms (indices 7-12: 9, 56, 318, 1013, 493, 173 ms) while typical is 2 ms. The route-log duration_ms for those same requests was only 0.6-2.7 ms, so the delay happened before the middleware started timing: the request sat waiting for the event loop. Something else was occupying the loop for up to ~1 s at that moment; the likeliest cause is a departures or stop-id journey from another client (consistent with the blocking probe), but the foreign request was not identified. It also shows that a client round trip can exceed the logged server duration by 1 s, so route-log duration_ms understates user latency under blocking.

LIMITS: sample sizes are small (6-40 per variant; 'p95' of 8 samples is nearly the max). Loopback removes network RTT; Docker Desktop on Windows has its own overheads (bind-mount over file sharing for the 3 GB SQLite on D:, NAT). Numbers rank costs on this machine; they do not predict Fargate absolutes. Realtime and alerts are not enabled, so no live-source latency was measured.
